data.reasoning: The package is a standard font package with no malicious behavior. The PKGBUILD contains only safe variable assignments at global scope, sources from the legitimate upstream (unifoundry.com) with SHA-256 checksums and PGP verification, and the package() function only installs font files and licenses. data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by tool/infrastructure errors, not substantive security concerns. qwen3-235b failed to audit .nvchecker.toml due to HTTP 400 error, and openrouter/free failed to audit .gitignore due to empty LLM response. These are transient failures, not security findings. deepseek-v4-flash successfully reviewed all 4 files and found them safe.
coverage_issues: qwen3-235b: .nvchecker.toml audit failed due to HTTP 400 BadRequestError
openrouter/free: .gitignore audit failed due to LLMResponseError (empty response)
learnings: Tool errors (API failures, empty responses) should not cause 'inconclusive' package verdicts when other files are safe and one model completed a full audit successfully
The audit system should distinguish between 'file audit failed due to tool error' and 'file contains suspicious content' - tool errors should be retried or noted separately from security verdicts

When a package has only 4 small files and one model successfully audits all of them finding no issues, while other models' failures are clearly infrastructure-related, the verdict should be 'safe' rather than 'inconclusive'
